text:
eli: Heads-up — I'm kicking off an experiment for adaptive eviction penalties to reduce hotkey ping-pong. Instead of a fixed penalty per eviction, we scale the penalty by a recent "access_factor" and tenant weight. want quick sanity-checks.

tara: sketch the math? quick example helps. :thinking_face:

eli: sketch: penalty = base_penalty * clamp(1 + log(1 + access_factor), 1, max_scale) * tenant_priority_factor
eli: access_factor = recent_hits / expected_hot_rate (sliding window 1m)

sam: two immediate concerns: starvation for low-priority tenants and weird interactions with prefetch. need cap + cooldown.

anika: agree. also we should track these metrics during the run: rehydrate_rate, rehydrate_latency_p95, eviction_churn_per_min, hotkey_shadow_hits.

eli: proposed safety knobs: 
```
evict.adaptive:
  enabled: true
  base_penalty_ms: 150
  max_scale: 8.0
  cooldown_window_s: 120
  tenant_scale_map:
    default: 1.0
    enterprise: 0.6
    free: 1.5
```

eli: Also adding an opt-in header for tenants to opt-out of aggressive scaling.

tara: how will this interact w/ prefix sharing? if two prefixes share slab, scaled penalties could push eviction to other prefixes. we need topology-aware attribution.

sam: topology-aware idea: compute slab-local access_factor and prefer intra-slab demotion. If cross-prefix eviction needed, account penalty debit to origin prefix.

anika: experiment plan: roll to 10% of serving fleet (canary), gather metrics for 24h, run offline sims against last-week trace to estimate tail regressions. AB compare to current fixed-penalty baseline.

eli: rollout checklist I'm thinking: build flag, canary config, metric dashboards (anika), automated rollback trigger if p95 rehydrate increases > 30% or churn doubles.

sam: + add a safety that denies increased penalty when prefetch predicts imminent reuse (prefetch_confidence > 0.7).

eli: runtime-bot: kicked off canary deployment (evict.adaptive=true) on 10% nodes for trace replay job #evict-cal-2026-01

runtime-bot: deploybot: canary started at 2026-03-21T14:05Z, nodes: 120, config: evict.adaptive (see run id evict-cal-2026-01).

tara: experiment success criteria we should surface to PL: net token-cost reduction, 99p rehydrate latency not regressing, fewer repeated evicts per-key.

anika: I'll add those to the dashboard and create an alert group.

eli: thanks — I'll pair w/ sam next week to run the offline sims and then we can schedule the canary. tagging @tara for ownership of the rollout doc. :thumbsup:
